LESSON: AREA

Grade: Grade 5
Subject: MATHEMATICS
Strand: Measurement
Topic 2.2: Area
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 6

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Area, part of Measurement in Grade 5 MATHEMATICS.

Key inquiry question: How can you determine the area of different surfaces?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

A. identify the square centimetre (cm2 ) as a unit of measuring area in real life,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Area in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

B. work out area of rectangles and squares in square centimetres (cm2 ) in different situations,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Area in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

C. appreciate the use of cm2 in working out area in real life.

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Area in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

A. identify the square centimetre (cm2 ) as a unit of measuring area in real life,

   Area helps learners achieve this outcome through discussion, practice, and activities at school. Think about how this applies in daily life in Kenya — at home, on the farm, in town, or at school.

B. work out area of rectangles and squares in square centimetres (cm2 ) in different situations,

   Area helps learners achieve this outcome through discussion, practice, and activities at school. Think about how this applies in daily life in Kenya — at home, on the farm, in town, or at school.

C. appreciate the use of cm2 in working out area in real life.

   Area helps learners achieve this outcome through discussion, practice, and activities at school. Think about how this applies in daily life in Kenya — at home, on the farm, in town, or at school.

D. Suggested learning experiences (from KICD)

1. discuss and measure, trace and cut out 1 cm by 1cm units, and refer the area of each as one square centimetre (1cm2 ),

2. cover a given surface using 1-centimetre square cut-outs and count the number of cut-outs to get the area in cm2 ,

3. establish the area of rectangles and squares in cm2 as the product of the number 1cm2 units in the row by the number of units in the column, area of rectangle or square = length x width,

4. team up with peers to play games involving area using multiplication charts.

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

1. discuss and measure, trace and cut out 1 cm by 1cm units, and refer the area of each as one square centimetre (1cm2 ),
2. cover a given surface using 1-centimetre square cut-outs and count the number of cut-outs to get the area in cm2 ,
3. establish the area of rectangles and squares in cm2 as the product of the number 1cm2 units in the row by the number of units in the column, area of rectangle or square = length x width,
4. team up with peers to play games involving area using multiplication charts.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Area together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Values:
Unity: learner teams up with peers to play games involving area using multiplication charts.

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
(PCIs):

Environmental awareness: learner covers a given surface from the environment using 1-centimetre square cut-outs and counts

the number of cut-outs to get the area in cm2

Link to other learning areas:

Learner relates concept of area to planting fields in Agriculture.

SECTION 6: SUMMARY

Main points to remember:

1. identify the square centimetre (cm2 ) as a unit of measuring area in real life,
2. work out area of rectangles and squares in square centimetres (cm2 ) in different situations,
3. appreciate the use of cm2 in working out area in real life.

Remember the key question: How can you determine the area of different surfaces?
